title: Ventilation Job Matcher
description: Learners recommend one of twelve product lines for each of twelve illustrative building ventilation jobs and name the deciding factor (air contents, discharge path, mounting location or occupant exposure). Both choices are marked with the reason after each commit, and a summary lists every job, the learner's choice and the correct choice, grouped by deciding factor.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Matching building ventilation jobs to product lines
learningObjectives: The learner will recommend the product line that fits each of twelve building ventilation jobs, judged by the air contents, discharge path, mounting location and occupant exposure described in the job.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts and summaries announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour in the feedback and the product line list; native select and buttons; keys 1-4 choose the factor, Enter commits or goes on.

Commit
controls.purpose: Commit both choices (Enter); one attempt per card

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Clear both scores and repeat the twelve cards in the session's order

rules: Twelve cards, shuffled once per session; each has exactly one correct product line and one correct deciding factor.
Product line and deciding factor are scored separately; mastery uses product lines only (10 of 12 on the first attempt).
One attempt per card, no re-answering; the correct answers are revealed after each commit.
assumptions: Job cards are illustrative scenarios written for chapter 5.
limitations: Does not size or select a model; the current catalog page for the chosen line supplies sizes and ratings.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge each job against four criteria and name the deciding one, so a correct guess for the wrong reason is caught
keyQuestions: Where must the air go, and where can the fan sit?
Are people standing in the airflow?
commonMisconceptions: Any roof exhauster can handle any exhaust air.
A smoke exhaust job only needs a large ordinary fan.
Stainless steel is the only answer for corrosive air.
A mancooler is an exhaust fan.
Every relief opening needs a powered fan.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'Product lines correct: n of 12'; mastery is 10 of 12 product lines on the first attempt. 'Reasons correct: n of 12' is shown separately.
